recent_posts.title: Xbox announces leadership changes as it stops development of Gaming Copilot for console
recent_posts.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has announced significant leadership changes, including the cancellation of Gaming Copilot for consoles and the phasing out of the feature on mobile. The move comes just months after Xbox announced Copilot would arrive on current-gen consoles in 2026. Several new executives from Microsoft's CoreAI division are joining Xbox, while existing leaders are being reassigned. The restructuring aims to help Xbox move faster, deepen community connections, and address friction for players and developers. Xbox also plans to expand into China and emerging markets, strengthen Game Pass, and focus on growing daily active users despite a 33% drop in hardware revenue in Q3.

recent_posts.title: Valve's 2026 hardware push from iterative experiments to mainstream ambition
recent_posts.summary: Valve's redesigned Steam Controller has launched to near-universal critical praise, setting a positive tone for the company's ambitious 2026 hardware lineup that also includes the Steam Machine home console and Steam Frame VR headset. The strong reception reflects years of trust-building with Steam customers and Valve's iterative hardware strategy — each device serving as both a product and a research programme. The Steam Controller benefits directly from Steam Deck's control ecosystem, while the Steam Machine builds on Proton's decade of Linux compatibility work. Despite solid critical reception, questions remain about mainstream commercial viability: the Controller's $99 price competes against cheaper first-party pads, and the Steam Machine's unsubsidized PC pricing may put it above PS5 territory. Valve's unique position as owner of ~75% of PC game distribution means 'niche success' is financially viable, but the company's hardware ambitions are now clearly growth vectors aimed at recruiting console and VR gamers into the Steam ecosystem.

recent_posts.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 wins Best Game at the BIG Festival Awards at Gamescom Latam
recent_posts.summary: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 by Sandfall Interactive won Best Game and Best Audio at the BIG Festival Awards held during Gamescom Latam in São Paulo, Brazil. Other category winners included Moomintroll: Winter's Warmth (Best Art), The Roottrees Are Dead (Best Narrative), and MIO: Memories In Orbit (Best Gameplay). The event also announced the shortlist for the 'Brazil is Ready for Gaming' Award, with the winner to be revealed at Gamescom in Germany in August, receiving a 70,000 Brazilian reals ($14,000) cash prize.

recent_posts.title: Brazil's game dev scene has the foundation but needs investment to break through
recent_posts.summary: Gamescom Latam 2026 in São Paulo highlights Brazil's growing game development scene, with strong infrastructure including a trade body (Abragames), a legal framework for games, and a thriving event attracting 130,000+ visitors. However, the industry's key missing ingredient is investment — particularly government tax incentives and grants. While Brazil excels in external/co-dev work and has a vibrant indie scene, AAA development is still emerging. Stories like Mandinga Games' creator, who leveraged an $8,000 government grant to go full-time and later secured $80,000 from ID@Xbox, illustrate how targeted funding can be transformative. Industry leaders see Brazil as a long-term bet, and local organizers argue that financial support is the final catalyst needed to unlock the region's full potential.

recent_posts.title: Roblox announces AI-driven upscaler called Roblox Reality
recent_posts.summary: Roblox has announced Roblox Reality, an AI-driven photorealism upscaler that layers AI-powered Video World Models on top of the existing Roblox Cloud and Game Engine. The technology aims to enhance lighting, textures, and motion rendering while significantly reducing development time, cost, and compute requirements for high-fidelity graphics. Roblox CEO David Baszucki described it as a hybrid architecture that could allow a small team to build a photorealistic game in a week. An early version is expected later in 2026 or early 2027, though scaling to millions of concurrent players remains a challenge the company is actively working to solve.

recent_posts.title: ESA's iicon was a promising start, but needs more commitment and more candour | Opinion
recent_posts.summary: The ESA's inaugural iicon event in Las Vegas marked a deliberate departure from E3's consumer-facing spectacle, targeting C-suite industry leaders with focused discussions on regulation, cultural impact, and transmedia strategy. While the attendee quality was high — featuring executives from EA, Take-Two, Ubisoft, Riot, Roblox, Amazon, and Netflix — the event felt smaller than intended, with Xbox, Nintendo, and Sony largely absent from the stage. Presentations were polished but lacked new insights or actionable takeaways, and most speakers avoided audience questions. The event shows promise as a serious industry forum but needs fuller participation from all major players and more candid, substantive dialogue to fulfill its potential.

recent_posts.title: Union claims Nacon's decision to shutter Spiders was a "premeditated and deliberate choice"
recent_posts.summary: French union STJV has called for a boycott of Nacon following the closure of Spiders studio, describing the shutdown as a premeditated and deliberate choice rather than a financial inevitability. The union alleges Nacon exploited its dual role as owner and sole client of Spiders, denying the studio royalties after GreedFall, seizing its liquid assets, cancelling project Dark without explanation, and blocking Spiders from seeking contracts with other publishers. 71 workers are affected. The closure follows a 2024 worker strike over mismanagement, a subsequent audit, and Nacon's broader court-supervised reorganisation that also saw three other subsidiaries file for insolvency.

recent_posts.title: Krafton Q1 revenue up 56.9% to $931m, driven by mobile content
recent_posts.summary: Krafton reported record Q1 2026 results with revenue up 56.9% year-on-year to $931 million and operating profit of $381.3 million. Mobile was the largest revenue segment at $477 million, driven by Battlegrounds Mobile India which saw a 17% increase in paying users. The PUBG franchise grew 24% YoY, surpassing $679 million. Krafton also reaffirmed its AI-first strategy focused on delivering differentiated gameplay experiences through AI.

recent_posts.title: Roblox reports strong Q1 growth, revises full-year forecast due to new saftey measures
recent_posts.summary: Roblox posted strong Q1 2026 results with revenue of $1.4 billion (up 39%), bookings of $1.4 billion (up 43%), and average DAUs rising 35% year-over-year to 132 million. Monthly unique payers grew 52% to 31 million. Despite the growth, the company revised its full-year outlook downward — expecting bookings growth of 8–12% and revenue growth of 20–25% — due to the rollout of mandatory age checks and new safety measures. Roblox also announced a 42% increase in its Developer Exchange (DevEx) rate for age-verified US players 18+, and launched a new subscription service, Roblox Plus, at $5/month.

recent_posts.title: Epic Games Store launches on iPhone in Japan
recent_posts.summary: The Epic Games Store has launched on iPhone in Japan following the enactment of Japan's Mobile Software Competition Act (MSCA) in December 2025, which mandates support for alternative app stores and payment options. However, Epic is only launching with its own titles (Fortnite, Rocket League Sideswipe) due to Apple's 5% Core Technology Commission fee and transaction reporting requirements, which Epic says deter third-party developers. Apple also requires a nine-step installation process for third-party stores in Japan. Epic is urging the Japan Fair Trade Commission to enforce the law and prohibit Apple's fees and friction tactics, continuing its long-running legal and regulatory battle with Apple that began in 2020.
